title: On the Convergence of Adam, Revisited
hook: A 2018 result showed Adam can fail to converge only in a specific hyperparameter regime. This paper shows it can fail for ANY choice — a flaw that spreads to AdamW, RMSProp, even Muon.
key_points: Reddi, Kale & Kumar (2018) showed Adam can fail to converge in online optimization when β1 < √β2 — a specific relationship between the decay parameters.
This paper shows a strictly weaker guarantee: projected Adam's average regret can stay bounded away from zero for ANY β1, β2 in [0,1).
The construction is a three-periodic sequence of linear functions on [-1,1] with slopes c, -1, -1, where c is only slightly larger than 2.
The same non-convergence result extends to AdamW, RMSProp, NAdam, Adan, AdaMax, and Muon.
It also holds for an i.i.d. (randomized) version of the three-periodic sequence, not just the fixed adversarial one.
content_html: Adam is the field's default optimizer, but its convergence guarantees have always had gaps. This paper closes one of them: it shows projected Adam can fail to converge for any choice of its moment-decay hyperparameters, not just the narrow regime prior work had flagged.
extra_html:
In 2018, Reddi, Kale, and Kumar showed Adam could fail to converge in online convex optimization when β1 < √β2 — a specific relationship between the two decay rates. Steven Heilman and Sampad Mohanty now prove a strictly stronger negative result: projected Adam's average regret can stay bounded away from zero for any β1, β2 in [0,1), using a similar three-periodic sequence of linear functions on [-1,1] with slopes c, -1, -1, where c only needs to be slightly larger than 2.

They extend the same construction to show non-convergence for AdamW, RMSProp, NAdam, Adan, AdaMax, and even Muon, plus a randomized (i.i.d.) version of the adversarial sequence. The takeaway isn't that Adam is broken in practice — it's that the theoretical convergence story for the whole family of adaptive optimizers is weaker than commonly assumed, and holds up worse than the specific 2018 counterexample suggested.

related.title: Adam: The Default Optimizer
related.hook: Adam gives every parameter its own adaptive step size by tracking the gradient's recent average and spread — and it mostly just works.

related.title: Muon: An Optimizer for Hidden Layers
related.hook: Muon orthogonalizes each gradient update before applying it — and trained networks faster than AdamW, the first serious challenger to Adam's reign in years.

related.title: AdamW: Decoupled Weight Decay
related.hook: L2 regularization and weight decay are the same thing for plain SGD - but not for Adam. Decoupling them fixes Adam's generalization and makes the best decay value independent of the learning rate.

flashcards.prompt: What did Reddi, Kale & Kumar (2018) show about Adam's convergence, and how does this paper go further?
flashcards.back_html: RKK showed Adam can fail to converge in online optimization when β1 < √β2. This paper shows non-convergence (average regret bounded away from zero) for ANY β1, β2 in [0,1) — no special relationship required.

flashcards.prompt: What construction does the paper use to prove Adam's average regret stays bounded away from zero?

choices.text: A three-periodic sequence of linear functions on [-1,1] with slopes c, -1, -1, where c is just above 2
A single non-differentiable function evaluated once
A randomly initialized deep network's training loss curve

flashcards.explanation_html: The adversarial online-optimization sequence cycles through three linear functions with slopes c, -1, -1 (c slightly above 2), which drives Adam's average regret away from zero for any moment-decay parameters.

flashcards.prompt: Beyond plain Adam, which other optimizers does the non-convergence result extend to?
flashcards.back_html: AdamW, RMSProp, NAdam, Adan, AdaMax, and Muon — plus an i.i.d. (randomized) variant of the adversarial sequence.
